ci_method: Visit-level OLS (linear probability model) of 14-day follow-up on program x post, SEs clustered at the practice level (CR1, 60 clusters), 95% interval from t(59). Confirmed by wild cluster bootstrap-t with Rademacher weights, B=2000 (95% percentile-t CI [5.91, 9.79], p=0.0005) and by randomization inference permuting program status across the 60 practices (B=2000, p=0.0005, null sd 1.42pp).

assumptions_checked: Parallel pre-trends, event study: program x month interactions for Jan-May 2025 (ref June) are -3.50, -3.94, -2.82, -2.89, +0.84pp; joint F-test that all pre-period interactions are zero F=1.49, p=0.208 (not rejected). The post-period jump (+8.7pp in July) is discrete and does not continue upward, which is inconsistent with a continuing trend.

Parallel pre-trends, linear version: differential pre-period slope = +0.909pp/month (se 0.402, p=0.027) - marginally significant, so I tested it four ways. (a) Estimated jointly with a jump, the trend collapses to +0.12pp/mo (n.s.) and the jump is +7.16pp; AIC/BIC prefer jump-only over trend-only. (b) It would take a differential trend of 1.32pp/month to fully explain the headline estimate, ~1 se above the already-noisy pre-period slope. (c) The narrow May-Jun vs Jul-Aug comparison, where trend bias is at most ~1.8pp, still gives +7.76pp. (d) Decomposing by channel, the hospital-based family-practice clinic channel carries +6.24pp of the effect and has a pre-trend of +0.09pp/mo (se 0.187) - a 1.04pp/month trend would be needed to explain it, over 5 se away. Conclusion: the apparent pre-trend is pre-period noise concentrated in the office channel, not a secular divergence.

Placebo / in-time falsification: fake 2025-04-01 launch within the pre-period gives +2.72pp (p=0.050) - borderline, reflecting the same noisy mid-pre-period wobble (the program-minus-control gap moves from about -7pp in Jan-Apr to -3.5pp in May-Jun); it is one third the size of the real estimate and of opposite implication to the sharp July break.

Outcome falsification: specialist-office follow-up within 14 days (-0.38pp, p=0.41) and lab use within 14 days (-0.09pp, p=0.82) show no program effect, so the result is not generic claim-volume or coding drift.

Composition of the ED denominator: ED volume per practice (DiD -1.37 visits, p=0.84), ED acuity mix (99281-99285 shares within 0.4pp across all four cells), unique ED members, and repeat-ED share are all balanced between groups and periods. Mild exception: PCP contact in the 14 days BEFORE the ED visit rose 1.12pp more in program practices (p=0.09), a small hint that program members became slightly more primary-care-connected.

Follow-up window censoring: ED visits run through 2025-12-31 and the extract runs through 2026-01-14, so every ED visit has its full 14-day window observed. Verified Jan 1-14 2026 claim flow is complete (18,683 professional and 3,494 facility lines; office-PCP and hospital-clinic visit counts are 0.448 and 0.442 of December's, vs the 14/31 = 0.452 expected), so December follow-ups are not undercounted.

ED visit definition: facility claims with POS 23 and revenue code 0450 - exactly 31,271 claims, each with one ED E&M line (99281-99285) and a matching professional ED claim for the same member-day (31,260 member-days, 100% overlap of the two sources, 11 member-days with two ED claims). No inpatient or observation claims exist in the extract, so no admitted-from-ED exclusion is possible or needed.

PCP visit definition (the single most consequential choice): primary care is delivered through two channels in this data - professional office E&M (POS 11, 99204/99212-99215) by Family or Internal Medicine (256,071 visits) AND hospital-based family-practice clinic visits (G0463 with revenue code 0517, POS 22; 64,293 visits, 20% of all primary care, 5,924 members who use that channel exclusively, only 373 member-days overlapping with an office visit). Counting only the professional channel understates the effect at +2.42pp; the main specification counts both. Specialist office E&M at POS 11 (Cardiology, GI, Derm, Endo, Ortho) is excluded from the PCP definition - including it changes little (+7.50pp).

Verified that the hospital-clinic effect is not a billing artifact: the added program follow-ups are spread across days 3-14 after the ED visit (not piled on day 0, which would indicate the ED encounter itself being re-billed as a clinic visit), and office-PCP visit volume in program practices did not fall after launch (10,539/9,617/10,507/10,046/10,231/10,063 before vs 10,375/10,482/10,068/10,408/10,084/10,479 after), so office visits were not relabelled as facility clinic visits.

Mechanism, with a caveat worth knowing: total hospital-clinic visit volume in program practices rose only ~3.5% after launch (15,251 to 17,062) while post-ED follow-up through that channel doubled (6.4% to 12.3%), i.e. the program largely re-prioritised existing primary care appointment slots toward recent ED patients rather than adding capacity.
Treatment timing: all 30 program practices have launch_date 2025-07-01, so this is a clean 2x2 DiD with no staggered adoption and no need for heterogeneity-robust estimators.

Data integrity: 1,067,719 lines, no duplicate rows, no duplicate claim_id+line_no, no zero or negative allowed amounts, no missing service dates, every claim has one member/date/practice/claim_type, each of the 119,560 members maps to exactly one of the 60 practices (so no attribution switching), and monthly claim volume is flat with no gaps.

Inference: 60 clusters is enough for cluster-t, but verified anyway with wild cluster bootstrap-t (p=0.0005) and randomization inference over program assignment (p=0.0005). Effect is broad-based, not driven by outlier practices: all 30 program practices improved (mean +8.69pp, range +1.8 to +14.2) versus 18 of 30 control practices (mean +0.86pp, range -8.6 to +8.4); leave-one-practice-out estimates span 7.52 to 8.13pp.
Functional form: LPM, logit (DiD of predicted probabilities) and practice-level collapsed means all give 7.8-7.9pp, so the linear model is not distorting the result.
headline_claim: The care-navigation program raised the 14-day ED-to-PCP follow-up rate by 7.9 percentage points (95% CI 5.9 to 9.8), from 29.4% to 38.2% in program practices while comparison practices were flat at about 35-36%, with every one of the 30 program practices improving.
